body.justification: Matching lower and feasible-estimator upper bounds hold over the same enlarged class with all donors used once.
body.gap: The proof allows heterogeneous bounded responses and design-only geometric beta mixing, and it uses no covariance estimator.
body.consumer: Designers can locate the active replication, spacing, or donor-precision channel.
body.proof_tex:
For channel \(q\), take \((P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\) from \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}, write its target values as \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), and put \(\Delta_q=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  The pair has affinity at least \(a_0>0\) and \(\Delta_q^2\ge cR_q\).  For any estimator \(\widetilde\tau\), the events
\[
E'_0=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_0|\ge\Delta_q/2\},
\qquad
E'_1=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_1|\ge\Delta_q/2\}
\]
cover the sample space.  Integrating against the overlap measure gives
\[
P_{0,q}(E'_0)+P_{1,q}(E'_1)\ge a_0,
\]
and hence
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}
[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_\ell)^2\mid E_0]
\ge\frac{a_0\Delta_q^2}{8}\ge cR_q.
\tag{50}
\]
Maximizing over the four channels and using \(R_{\star,\beta}=\max_qR_q\), then taking the supremum over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\) and the infimum over estimators, proves the lower bound.

For the upper bound put \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,t\le T\}\), and condition on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  On the event of successful fits, \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and the linear representation in \texttt{def:honest-interval} give
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=U_{\mathrm{evt}}-U_{\mathrm{hist}}-B_{\mathrm{LP}}-B_{\mathrm{don}},
\tag{51}
\]
where
\[
U_{\mathrm{evt}}=\sum_{s,i}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\},
\qquad
U_{\mathrm{hist}}=\sum_{s,i}\pi_s\sum_t a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti},
\]
\[
B_{\mathrm{LP}}=\sum_s\pi_s
\left\{\sum_{t,i}a_{sti}m_s(X_{st})-m_s(\widetilde z_s)\right\},
\qquad
B_{\mathrm{don}}=\sum_s\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
The two full-design restrictions center the first two sums under the displayed conditioning.  Conditional cross-unit independence and the range bound \(B\) yield
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{evt}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
\le B^2\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=B^2R_{\mathrm{tr}},
\tag{52}
\]
and \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} yields
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{hist}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
\le B^2\sum_{s,i}\left[\pi_s\sum_t|a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le B^2c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{53}
\]
The entire calendar response path of one unit is one cluster in (53); no temporal outcome restriction or identical unit law is used.

If \(C_K\) bounds the Euclidean radius of the kernel support, then \(\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2\le C_Kh_s\) whenever \(w_{st}>0\).  The deterministic weight bound and the Holder Taylor remainder give
\[
|B_{\mathrm{LP}}|\le C\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\tag{54}
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz, \((\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda)^2\le S\sum_s\pi_s^2h_s^{2\lambda}\).  Apply \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(2\lambda\).  Since \(S\) and the positive weights are fixed,
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{LP}}^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}+N^{-\lambda}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta},
\tag{55}
\]
where \(N^{-\lambda}\le N^{-\kappa}\) because \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

Put
\[
W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{N}Y_j,
\qquad Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0).
\]
Donor replication gives independent mean-zero vectors satisfying \(\mathbb E[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Expanding \(\|W_N\|_2^4\), all terms with a singleton index vanish.  The all-equal terms and the three pairings give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
&=\frac1N\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-\frac1N\right)
\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\}\\
&\le \frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)=M_4(N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{56}
\]
Consequently
\[
\mathbb E_P\left[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2^4\mid E_0\right]
\le CN^{-2}.
\tag{57}
\]
Euclidean projection onto the cube cannot increase distance from \(z_0\), and the eigenvalue bounds imply
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2.
\tag{58}
\]
On the event where the left side of (58) is at most \(\delta_0\), the upper local-modulus inequality bounds \(|B_{\mathrm{don}}|^2\) by its \(2\kappa\)-th power times a fixed constant.  Lyapunov's inequality and (57) bound the expectation by \(CN^{-\kappa}\).  On the complementary event, boundedness gives \(|B_{\mathrm{don}}|\le B\), while Markov's inequality and (57) give probability \(O(N^{-2})\).  Since \(0<\kappa\le1\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{don}}^2\mid E_0]
\le CN^{-\kappa}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{59}
\]

Every successful intercept has absolute value at most \(B\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|\le Bc_G^{-1/2}\), and failed intercepts are zero.  Hence squared error is uniformly bounded on the bad sample.  The bad-sample bound in the selector lemma makes its contribution at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\).  Combining (51)--(59) with \((x_1+\cdots+x_4)^2\le4\sum_jx_j^2\) proves
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le CR_{\star,\beta}.
\tag{60}
\]
The same quantity upper-bounds the minimax infimum because \(\widehat\tau\) is a single observed-data estimator.

For completeness, let \(a=2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)\).  For every \(T\ge3\), weighted arithmetic--geometric mean and \(\log T\ge1\) give
\[
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-2\lambda/d})^{1-a}
\le an_s^{-1}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\]
After multiplying by \(\pi_s^2\), summing, and using \(\sum_s\pi_s^2\le1\),
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\le aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{61}
\]
Thus \(R_{\star,\beta}=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\) exactly for \(T\ge3\).  Equations (50) and (60) establish the asserted same-class bracket in every relative-growth regime.  The full donor covariance enters through the standardized modulus and (58), but neither the estimator nor the proof estimates it.
